newsitem.title: USA: Georgia man pleads innocent to college rapes.
newsitem.headline: Georgia man pleads innocent to college rapes.

text.p: A convicted rapist who police say attacked 11 college-age women in Florida and Georgia after his release from prison has pleaded innocent to charges he sexually assaulted five University of Georgia students during a one-year period.
John Alexander Scieszka Jr. pleaded not guilty Tuesday to 17 felony charges stemming from five alleged sexual assaults in an Athens residential neighbourhood adjacent to the university campus.

It was Scieszka's first court appearance since he was arrested Jan. 30 on a Florida warrant charging him with sexual battery in an alleged July 1995 attack on a University of Florida student who was jogging near campus.

Scieszka has been held without bond since being indicted on 17 felony counts of burglary, aggravated assault, rape, aggravated sodomy and aggravated sexual battery. The alleged incidents occurred in Athens between March 1995 and March 1966.

The 46-year-old Scieszka served almost 12 years in the Florida prison system after being convicted of raping two young women in 1980. He also faces sexual assault charges involving six other women in Atlanta, Valdosta, Georgia, and Gainesville, Florida.
Judge Lawton Stephens gave Scieszka's attorney 30 days to file motions in the case.
